header:
Meeting: SLA thresholds, keying, and rollback playbook review
Date: 2026-08-27 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Oliver Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Kumar (Redwood CSM); Sofia Alvarez (Trellis Procurement), Rajesh Nair (Trellis Security), Lena Ortiz (Trellis Cloud), Markus Voss (Trellis Legal)
summary: High-level procurement + security review focused on SLA floor/ceiling thresholds, KMS customer-managed keying options, and an operational rollback/playbook for Canary and major incidents. Customer requested concrete artifacts: redlined MSA/DPA, a 24h performance benchmark comparing Dedicated vs Hosted modes, and an explicit on-call/escalation appendix for the SLA. Concerns around EU data residency, key custody and audit log fidelity were raised.
topics: MSA redlines; DPA data residency options; SLA uptime vs latency vs burst capacity; dedicated vs hosted performance tradeoffs; customer-managed KMS/HSM options; rollback/canary runbook; pricing impact of burst and reserved capacity; audit logs and egress fees
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay, thanks everyone for carving out time. quick agenda — go through sla thresholds, key-management options, and the rollback playbook. is that right sofia?
[00:12] Sofia: yes, that's right. procurement wants clarity on the commercial path but security will drive the KMS and data residency asks.
[00:22] Oliver: I'll start with a short primer on how Redwood Dedicated differs from hosted from an operational perspective — sorry for any transcripshun typos, just it's live. so Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool, predictable throughput, you can pin model versions and use customer VPC peering. Hosted is our multi-tenant offering with burst capacity but shared infra.
[00:45] Lena: can you quantify cold-starts on Dedicated vs Hosted? we have a couple customer journeys that are latency-sensitive during opening hours.
[00:52] Oliver: good question. ballpark we've seen 50-150ms variance per request on steady-state token generation; cold-starts for new model containers could be seconds depending on batch and kv-cache warmup. we'll run a 24h workload that mirrors your 8k-token flow and share numbers.
[01:12] Rajesh: important for us is key custody. we require customer-managed keys for PII-derived prompts in EU region. how is that supported? 
[01:20] Maya: we support KMS integrations — cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) and HSM via bring-your-own-key. for Private deployments we can provide the control plane in your VPC and we never persist plaintext data outside your network by default.
[01:35] Markus: legal wants to understand liability and the SLA credits mechanism. the draft SLA in your deck lists a 99.9% uptime with credits, but the bank needs a clear escalation ladder for partial outages.
[01:48] Priya: absolutely — we can provide a detailed escalation appendix. typical flow is on-call -> SE -> infra escalation -> executive notice. we can also define severity levels and response windows, e.g., sev1 — 15 min ack, 1 hour mitigation plan.
[02:10] Sofia: and what about rollback? if a new model version causes hallucination or latency spikes, we need a guaranteed rollback path and easy ops steps.
[02:20] Oliver: our rollout tooling supports canary traffic split and automatic rollback triggers — threshold-based (latency, error-rate, quality regressions). SE will provide a runbook with exact curl examples for invoking rollback and automated fallback to a compatible variant.
[02:38] Rajesh: is telemetry and audit log accessible for our SIEM? we need token-level traceability, not just aggregated metrics.
[02:45] Maya: yes, audit logs including request IDs, model version, region, timestamp, and KMS key ID can be forwarded to your cloud logging bucket. retention windows are configurable; standard is 90 days but enterprise tier can extend.
[03:05] Lena: any egress fee implications for EU data residency? if we host in eu-west and egress to us for backups, there will be transfer charges and legal gets nervous about cross-border backups.
[03:17] Markus: correct, we need to avoid unintentional cross-border persistence. the DPA should state residency constraints.
[03:24] Maya: we'll include explicit data residency clauses in the DPA and an architecture appendix showing where backups live. for Private deployments you can control backup locations.
[03:35] Sofia: pricing — reserved dedicated capacity is attractive but procurement needs visibility on burst fees and overruns. we frequently have opening-day spikes.
[03:44] Maya: pricing model options: monthly reserved commits with defined burst buckets, or hosted pay-as-you-go. burst is billed at a defined uplift per token or per vGPU-hour depending on the plan; we'll send a rate sheet.
[03:56] Rajesh: any third-party validation — SOC2, iso27001? we need audit artifacts.
[04:00] Priya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we've started ISO work. we can share our attestation, pen-test summary, and a sample SOC2 report under NDA.
[04:12] Oliver: technical deep-dive aside: if you expect sub-100ms tail latency we recommend colocated Dedicated with KV-cache priming and pinned model variants to avoid cold starts.
[04:26] Lena: can we get a run at a canary where we route 5% of production traffic for one week, metrics observed, then move to 25% etc. who owns rollback?
[04:34] Maya: Redwood SE will partner with your Cloud ops for the canary. rollback is a joint action — Redwood can flip the routing but you'll have final cutover authority. we'll put the acceptance gate in the runbook.
[04:50] Markus: contractually we need SLA credits that are meaningful, not token discounts. also, an exceptions process for operational maintenance windows should be explicit — we can't have surprise downtimes.
[04:59] Maya: we'll move to include a maintenance window schedule and notification window — standard 72h notice for planned work, emergency maint limited with exec notice.
[05:12] Sofia: last, procurement asks for a sample invoice layout and termination clause with data deletion certifications.
[05:20] Maya: yes, we'll include an invoice sample and a data destruction certificate template as attachment to the DPA.
[05:28] Priya: recap — action items: redlined MSA + DPA by redwood legal; se benchmark for Dedicated vs Hosted (24h test); runbook for canary/rollback; redwood to send SOC2 artifact under NDA.
[05:40] Markus: timeline wise, legal wants a 2 week review window once redlines are received.
[05:45] Maya: sounds good. is there anything else?
[05:48] Rajesh: just one more note — our key rotation policy is every 90 days and we need proof that key revocation doesn't orphan persisted tokens.
[05:58] Oliver: we will document key rotation flows and test revocation scenarios in the KMS appendix.
[06:05] Maya: perfect, we'll follow up with docs and schedule the benchmark. thanks everyone.
notes: Customer stressed need for explicit rollback SLA and for audit-level logs. Legal wants credits spelled out; procurement asked for invoice samples and termination/data deletion attestation. SE recommended Dedicated for tight latency constraints and KV priming. KMS and EU residency are gating items.
final_recap: Maya to send redlines and commercial terms; Oliver to run bench; Priya to send rollback runbook. Trellis to confirm stakeholders for security signoff and to review redlines within two weeks.
